children.explain: Server push lets servers send resources to clients before they are requested. This prevents blocking caused by un-loadable resources.

children.example: A web server pushing CSS files to a browser before the HTML requests them.
children.exercise: Describe a scenario where server push would improve initial page load time.

children.explain: HTTP messages include a request message from the client and a response from the server.
children.mechanism: 1. Client sends a request message. 2. Server processes the request. 3. Server sends a response message.

children.mechanism: 1. Identify the resource using a URI. 2. Select an appropriate method (e.g., GET). 3. Include necessary message headers.
children.example: Requesting a specific user profile page on a website.
